title: Understanding KDE
text: A Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) is a way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable. It should be smooth and the area under the curve should equal $$1$$.

title: Checking the Area Under the Curve
text: To determine if the KDE is valid, consider whether the total area under the curve equals $$1$$. This is a key property of probability density functions.

hintAnswer: No, because the curve has negative density values.

text: Does the curve appear to have any negative values, or does it stay above the x-axis?
choices: Yes, because the curve is smooth and unimodal.
No, because the curve has negative density values.
